threads.body: Feels inefficient. It needs to loop over `registeredObservables` list to remove each element while previously it looped only once.

[General] Keep the whole replacement lifecycle serialized. Releasing the bookkeeping lock before cleanup and then reacquiring it only for this add lets `close()` snapshot and finish in between; the replacement is then registered after reporter shutdown has returned. Overlapping cleanup paths can also snapshot and close the same `AutoCloseable` twice (which is not required to be idempotent). Use a separate lifecycle/cleanup lock or an explicit claim protocol to serialize select → close → remove → add while leaving the bookkeeping lock free during `close()`, and add an overlap test for this interleaving.

replies.body:
Kafka already serializes `metricChange()` and `metricRemoval()` through synchronized methods on its `Metrics` instance. For normal shutdown, the producer joins its sender thread before closing metrics; the classic consumer rejects concurrent operations, and the async consumer joins its network thread before closing metrics. I haven't found a supported replacement-versus-shutdown interleaving that requires another lifecycle lock.

The observables here are `ObservableDoubleGauge` and `ObservableDoubleCounter`, whose `close()` contracts explicitly state that subsequent calls have no effect. The generic `AutoCloseable` contract isn't the applicable contract.

Leaving the implementation as-is. A concrete Kafka lifecycle path demonstrating overlap would be needed to justify additional synchronization.
